# What this report does

The noise-free SEIR and SIR BiLSTMs (trained on 1,000,000 simulated epidemics) and four
**standard calibration methods** (ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, DE and Nelder-Mead; settings
below and in `methods_common.R`) estimate R0 and the starting state from windows of real
daily counts: **30, 60 and 90 days** at the **beginning**, **middle** (centred on the peak)
and **end** of each epidemic wave.

Real data have no true R0, so methods are compared by how well their simulated curves match
the observed counts. Each method's estimates are run `r params$n_reps` times in
`ModelSEIRCONN` / `ModelSIRCONN` from the estimated starting state; each day's simulated
count is the number of people who became infectious that day (E -> I for SEIR, S -> I for
SIR).

- **Coverage**: the share of observed days inside the 95% band of those runs (higher is better).
- **Interval score**: band width plus 40 times how far each observed day falls outside the
  band (lower is better; a method cannot win it by making its band very wide).
- **Prediction**: coverage of the `r params$horizon` days after the window, where the data go on.
- **Time**: seconds and model runs per window.

| Method | Library | Settings (all defaults unless stated) | Model runs per window |
|---|---|---|---|
| BiLSTM | trained network (this package) | average of 5 trained networks; R0 range from 500 similar calibration windows | none (one network pass) |
| ABC-MCMC | this package (`make_calibrator("ABC-MCMC")`) | default: 3,000 random-walk steps (1,500 burn-in), proposal sd 8% of each range, Gaussian kernel with tolerance 0.30 x the root mean square of the observed counts | 3,000 |
| ABC-SMC | this package (`make_calibrator("ABC-SMC")`) | default: 200 particles, 6 generations, each tolerance the median distance of the previous generation; only its limits raised to 30,000 model runs and 20,000 attempts per generation (the defaults, 8,000 and 5,000, stopped it on many windows); a window where it still runs out is recorded as failed | up to 30,000 |
| DE | `DEoptim` | default: population 10 x number of unknowns, 200 generations, F = 0.8, CR = 0.5 | 6,000 (SIR) to 8,000 (SEIR) |
| Nelder-Mead | `stats::optim` | default: start at the middle of the ranges, up to 500 iterations; values outside the ranges rejected | until it stops |

All methods get the same windows, known values and ranges: R0 between 0.8 and 5, and the
state on the first day of the window (shares exposed (SEIR), infectious and recovered; the
baselines search them on the log10 scale between 0.0001 and 0.4, 0.95 for recovered), with
the contact rate fixed at the middle of its training range. The baselines fit the sum of
squared differences between the observed counts and the model's daily new infections; DE and
Nelder-Mead use one model run with a fixed seed per candidate.

```{r settings}
OUT_DIR <- params$out_dir
CORES   <- as.integer(params$cores)
LENGTHS <- as.integer(strsplit(params$lengths, ",")[[1]])
SEEDS   <- as.integer(strsplit(params$seeds, ",")[[1]])
H       <- as.integer(params$horizon)
N_REPS  <- as.integer(params$n_reps)
POSITIONS <- c("beginning", "middle", "end")
L_SHOW <- if (60 %in% LENGTHS) 60L else LENGTHS[1]   # window length shown in the example figures
METHODS <- c("BiLSTM", BASELINES)
specs <- strsplit(strsplit(params$model_dirs, ";")[[1]], "=")
MODEL_DIRS <- setNames(vapply(specs, `[`, "", 2), vapply(specs, `[`, "", 1))
INFO <- lapply(setNames(names(MODEL_DIRS), names(MODEL_DIRS)), model_info)
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(normalizePath(OUT_DIR), "figures", ""))
run_dir <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "method_runs"); dir.create(run_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
fit_dir <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "fits");        dir.create(fit_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
tab <- function(x, digits = 1, ...) knitr::kable(x, format = "html", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE,
                                                table.attr = "class='table table-condensed' style='width:auto'", ...)
```

# The data and the windows

**US states.** Daily new COVID-19 cases from the Johns Hopkins University repository (county
reports added up per state) for the `r params$n_states` states that reported cases every day,
with no negative corrections, in all three waves (states that skipped weekends have zeros on
about 30% of the days, which a noise-free model reads as no new infections). Cases are scaled
to cases per 10,000 people and the models use `n = 10,000`.

**Utah and Baltimore.** Utah COVID-19 cases (the last 365 days of the Utah data, and the
summer 2023 wave), Utah influenza hospital admissions (2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons) and
Baltimore influenza cases in 1918, with the population sizes used before.

Known values: COVID-19 `recov` = 1/7, `incub` = 5 days; influenza `recov` = 0.25,
`incub` = 2 days. Windows longer than a wave are skipped.

```{r data}
DD <- params$data_dir
st  <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "state_covid_daily_cases_jhu.csv")); st$date <- as.Date(st$date)
pop <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "state_population.csv"))
covid <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "utah_covid_all_days.csv")); covid$Date <- as.Date(covid$Date)
hhs <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "utah_hhs_hospital_admissions.csv")); hhs$date <- as.Date(substr(hhs$date, 1, 10)) - 1
e1918 <- new.env(); load(file.path(DD, "Flu1918.rda"), envir = e1918)
COVID <- list(recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5); FLU <- list(recov = 0.25, incub = 2)

# A wave: the full daily series (x, y), the days that make up the wave, n and the known values.
make_wave <- function(group, name, x, y, from, to, n, known) {
  idx <- which(x >= from & x <= to)
  list(group = group, name = name, x = x, y = as.numeric(y), idx = idx, n = n, known = known)
}
# The part of a season with the peak: between the last week without cases before the
# peak and the first one after it (as in the earlier real-data report).
season_range <- function(x, y, from, to) {
  s <- which(x >= as.Date(from) & x <= as.Date(to)); z <- y[s]
  ma <- as.numeric(stats::filter(z, rep(1 / 7, 7), sides = 2)); pk <- which.max(ma)
  zero_week <- vapply(seq_along(z), function(i) i >= 7 && all(z[(i - 6):i] == 0), logical(1))
  first <- max(c(0, which(zero_week & seq_along(z) < pk))) + 1
  after <- which(zero_week & seq_along(z) > pk)
  last <- if (length(after)) after[1] - 7 else length(z)
  x[s][c(first, last)]
}

STATES_USED <- head(c("California", "Colorado", "Delaware", "Maryland", "New Jersey", "New York", "North Dakota",
                      "Pennsylvania", "Tennessee", "Texas"), params$n_states)
STATE_WAVES <- list(`fall 2020` = c("2020-09-01", "2021-02-28"), `Delta 2021` = c("2021-06-15", "2021-11-30"),
                    `Omicron 2021-22` = c("2021-12-01", "2022-03-31"))
waves <- list()
for (s in STATES_USED) {
  d <- st[st$state == s, ]
  y <- round(d$daily_cases * 10000 / pop$population[pop$state == s])
  for (wv in names(STATE_WAVES))
    waves[[paste(s, wv)]] <- make_wave("US states", paste(s, wv), d$date, y, as.Date(STATE_WAVES[[wv]][1]),
                                       as.Date(STATE_WAVES[[wv]][2]), 10000, COVID)
}
flu <- hhs$previous_day_admission_influenza_confirmed
r22 <- season_range(hhs$date, flu, "2022-09-01", "2023-05-31")
r23 <- season_range(hhs$date, flu, "2023-09-01", "2024-04-26")
r_s <- season_range(covid$Date, covid$Daily.Cases, "2023-06-01", "2023-10-15")
last365 <- tail(covid$Date, 365)
OTHER <- list(
  make_wave("Utah and Baltimore", "Utah COVID-19 2024-25", covid$Date, covid$Daily.Cases, last365[1], last365[365], 5000, COVID),
  make_wave("Utah and Baltimore", "Utah flu 2022-23", hhs$date, flu, r22[1], r22[2], 5000, FLU),
  make_wave("Utah and Baltimore", "Utah flu 2023-24", hhs$date, flu, r23[1], r23[2], 5000, FLU),
  make_wave("Utah and Baltimore", "Baltimore flu 1918", seq_along(e1918$Flu1918$incidence), e1918$Flu1918$incidence,
            1, length(e1918$Flu1918$incidence), 10000, FLU),
  make_wave("Utah and Baltimore", "Utah COVID-19 summer 2023", covid$Date, covid$Daily.Cases, r_s[1], r_s[2], 10000, COVID))
for (v in OTHER) waves[[v$name]] <- v

windows <- list()
for (v in waves) {
  wy <- v$y[v$idx]
  ma <- as.numeric(stats::filter(wy, rep(1 / 7, 7), sides = 2)); pk <- which.max(ma)
  for (L in LENGTHS) {
    if (L > length(v$idx)) next
    for (pos in POSITIONS) {
      s0 <- switch(pos, beginning = 1, end = length(wy) - L + 1, middle = min(max(1, pk - floor(L / 2)), length(wy) - L + 1))
      at <- v$idx[s0:(s0 + L - 1)]
      fut <- at[L] + seq_len(H); fut <- fut[fut <= length(v$y)]
      id <- sprintf("w%03d", length(windows) + 1)
      windows[[id]] <- list(id = id, group = v$group, wave = v$name, length = L, position = pos, x = v$x[at],
                            y = v$y[at], future = v$y[fut], known = c(list(n = v$n), v$known))
    }
  }
}
saveRDS(windows, file.path(OUT_DIR, "windows.rds"))
saveRDS(lapply(waves, function(v) list(group = v$group, name = v$name, x = v$x[v$idx], y = v$y[v$idx])),
        file.path(OUT_DIR, "waves.rds"))
wt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(windows, function(w) data.frame(group = w$group, length = w$length, position = w$position)))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(table(paste(wt$group, wt$length, "days"), wt$position))[, POSITIONS],
             caption = "Number of windows per model, by data group and window length (rows) and position (columns)")
```

```{r data-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=19, fig.cap="Daily counts in each wave (blue; states: cases per 10,000 people). Grey bars: the 60-day windows at the beginning, middle and end."}
op <- par(mfrow = c(ceiling(length(waves) / 3), 3), mar = c(2, 4, 2, 0.5))
for (v in waves) {
  plot(v$x[v$idx], v$y[v$idx], type = "l", col = "blue", xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", main = v$name, cex.main = 0.9)
  usr <- par("usr")
  for (j in seq_along(POSITIONS)) {
    w <- Filter(function(z) z$wave == v$name && z$length == L_SHOW && z$position == POSITIONS[j], windows)
    if (!length(w)) next
    w <- w[[1]]; yy <- usr[4] - j * (usr[4] - usr[3]) * 0.05
    segments(w$x[1], yy, w$x[w$length], yy, lwd = 3, col = "grey40")
  }
}
par(op)
```

```{r baselines}
unit_file <- function(M, id, m) file.path(run_dir, sprintf("%s_%s_%s.rds", M, id, m))
units <- expand.grid(model = names(MODEL_DIRS), id = names(windows), method = BASELINES, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
units$days <- vapply(units$id, function(i) windows[[i]]$length, 0)
units <- units[order(match(units$method, c("DE", "ABC-SMC", "ABC-MCMC", "NelderMead")), -units$days), ]
units <- units[!file.exists(unit_file(units$model, units$id, units$method)), ]
if (nrow(units)) {
  done <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(units)), function(k) try({
    w <- windows[[units$id[k]]]; M <- units$model[k]
    saveRDS(fit_baseline(units$method[k], w$y, INFO[[M]], w$known[INFO[[M]]$known]), unit_file(M, w$id, units$method[k]))
  }), mc.cores = CORES, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
  bad <- vapply(done, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
  if (any(bad)) stop("Failed: ", paste(units$model[bad], units$id[bad], units$method[bad], collapse = "; "))
}
cat("Saved baseline fits:", length(list.files(run_dir)), "of", length(MODEL_DIRS) * length(windows) * length(BASELINES), "\n")
```

```{r bilstm}
bil_file <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "bilstm_fits.rds")
if (!file.exists(bil_file)) {
  set.seed(1)
  bil <- list()
  for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) {
    f <- make_bilstm(INFO[[M]], MODEL_DIRS[[M]], SEEDS, device = params$device)
    out <- f(lapply(windows, `[[`, "y"), do.call(rbind, lapply(windows, function(w) as.data.frame(w$known[INFO[[M]]$known]))))
    bil[paste(M, names(windows))] <- out
  }
  saveRDS(bil, bil_file)
}
bil <- readRDS(bil_file)
```

```{r bands}
fit_file <- function(M, id, m) file.path(fit_dir, sprintf("%s_%s_%s.rds", M, id, m))
fit_of <- function(M, id, m) if (m == "BiLSTM") bil[[paste(M, id)]] else readRDS(unit_file(M, id, m))
jobs <- expand.grid(model = names(MODEL_DIRS), id = names(windows), method = METHODS, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
todo <- which(!file.exists(fit_file(jobs$model, jobs$id, jobs$method)))
if (length(todo)) {
  done <- parallel::mclapply(todo, function(k) try({
    set.seed(k)
    M <- jobs$model[k]; w <- windows[[jobs$id[k]]]; m <- jobs$method[k]
    nf <- length(w$future)
    f <- fit_of(M, w$id, m)
    if (isTRUE(f$failed)) { saveRDS(list(failed = TRUE), fit_file(M, w$id, m)); return(NULL) }
    b <- band_of(INFO[[M]], f$draws, w$length + nf, n = N_REPS)
    saveRDS(list(band = b$new, window = score_band(b$new, w$y, seq_len(w$length)),
                 future = if (nf) score_band(b$new, w$future, w$length + seq_len(nf)) else NULL), fit_file(M, w$id, m))
  }), mc.cores = CORES, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
  bad <- vapply(done, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
  if (any(bad)) stop("Failed bands: ", sum(bad))
}
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(k) {
  M <- jobs$model[k]; w <- windows[[jobs$id[k]]]; m <- jobs$method[k]
  f <- fit_of(M, w$id, m); s <- readRDS(fit_file(M, w$id, m))
  if (isTRUE(f$failed)) return(data.frame(model = M, id = w$id, group = w$group, wave = w$wave, length = w$length,
    position = w$position, method = m, R0 = NA, R0_low = NA, R0_high = NA, coverage = NA, interval_score = NA, MAE = NA,
    width = NA, cov_future = NA, is_future = NA, seconds = f$seconds, model_runs = NA, failed = TRUE))
  data.frame(model = M, id = w$id, group = w$group, wave = w$wave, length = w$length, position = w$position, method = m,
             R0 = f$R0, R0_low = f$R0_low, R0_high = f$R0_high,
             coverage = s$window[["coverage"]], interval_score = s$window[["interval_score"]], MAE = s$window[["MAE"]],
             width = s$window[["width"]],
             cov_future = if (is.null(s$future)) NA else s$future[["coverage"]],
             is_future = if (is.null(s$future)) NA else s$future[["interval_score"]],
             seconds = f$seconds, model_runs = f$model_runs, failed = FALSE)
}))
write.csv(res, file.path(OUT_DIR, "results_by_window.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
all_res <- res
res <- res[!res$failed, ]   # the tables below use the windows where a method worked
```

# Results

How to read the tables:

- **Overall**: one row per model, data group and method, averaged over **all** windows of the
  group (every wave, window length and position): `r sum(vapply(windows, function(w) w$group == "US states", logical(1)))`
  windows for the US states, `r sum(vapply(windows, function(w) w$group != "US states", logical(1)))` for Utah and Baltimore.
- **By window length and position**: the same, split by window length and by where the window
  sits in the wave (beginning, middle around the peak, end).
- **By wave**: one row per wave (for example "New York fall 2020"), averaged over its windows
  (3 lengths x 3 positions = 9 windows, fewer for short waves). "Utah COVID-19 2024-25" is the
  last year of the Utah data rather than a single wave.
- Methods that failed on a window (ABC-SMC when it runs out of model runs) are averaged over
  the windows where they worked; the number of failures is given in the overall table.

## Overall

```{r overall, results="asis"}
ov <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(MODEL_DIRS), function(M) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("US states", "Utah and Baltimore"), function(g)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(METHODS, function(m) {
    d <- res[res$model == M & res$group == g & res$method == m, ]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(Model = M, Data = g, Method = m,
               `Windows (failed)` = sprintf("%d (%d)", nrow(d), sum(all_res$failed[all_res$model == M & all_res$group == g & all_res$method == m])),
               `Coverage (%)` = mean(d$coverage),
               `Interval score` = mean(d$interval_score), `Band width` = mean(d$width), `Error of the median` = mean(d$MAE),
               `Coverage: next 14 days (%)` = mean(d$cov_future, na.rm = TRUE),
               `Seconds per window` = mean(d$seconds), `Model runs per window` = mean(d$model_runs), check.names = FALSE)
  }))))))
write.csv(ov, file.path(OUT_DIR, "summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
ov$Model[duplicated(ov$Model)] <- ""
cat(tab(ov, caption = "Mean over all windows of each data group. States: counts per 10,000 people."), sep = "\n")
```

## By window length and position

```{r cell, results="asis"}
cell_table <- function(M, g, what) {
  a <- aggregate(as.formula(paste(what, "~ position + length + method")), res[res$model == M & res$group == g, ], mean)
  w <- reshape(a, idvar = c("position", "length"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub(paste0("^", what, "\\."), "", names(w))
  w <- w[order(match(w$position, POSITIONS), w$length), c("position", "length", intersect(METHODS, names(w)))]
  names(w)[1:2] <- c("Position", "Window (days)")
  w$Position[duplicated(w$Position)] <- ""
  w
}
for (g in c("US states", "Utah and Baltimore")) for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) {
  cat(tab(cell_table(M, g, "coverage"), digits = 0,
          caption = sprintf("%s, %s: coverage (%%) of the observed daily counts", M, g)), sep = "\n")
}
```

```{r cell-fig, fig.width=13, fig.height=8, fig.cap="US states: coverage by window length for windows at the beginning, middle and end of the waves (mean over the state waves). Dashed: 95%."}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) for (pos in POSITIONS) {
  a <- aggregate(coverage ~ length + method, res[res$model == M & res$group == "US states" & res$position == pos, ], mean)
  plot(NA, xlim = range(LENGTHS), ylim = c(0, 100), xlab = "window length (days)", ylab = "coverage %", main = paste(M, "-", pos))
  abline(h = 95, lty = 2)
  for (m in METHODS) {
    x <- a[a$method == m, ]; x <- x[order(x$length), ]
    lines(x$length, x$coverage, type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = if (m == "BiLSTM") 3 else 1.5, col = METHOD_COLS[[m]])
  }
  if (M == names(MODEL_DIRS)[1] && pos == "beginning") legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = METHOD_COLS[METHODS], legend = METHODS)
}
par(op)
```

Interval score (lower is better):

```{r cell-is, results="asis"}
for (g in c("US states", "Utah and Baltimore")) for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) {
  cat(tab(cell_table(M, g, "interval_score"), digits = 1,
          caption = sprintf("%s, %s: interval score", M, g)), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Prediction: the 14 days after the window

```{r future, results="asis"}
for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) {
  d <- res[res$model == M & !is.na(res$cov_future), ]
  a <- aggregate(cov_future ~ group + position + method, d, mean)
  w <- reshape(a, idvar = c("group", "position"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("^cov_future\\.", "", names(w))
  w <- w[order(w$group, match(w$position, POSITIONS)), c("group", "position", intersect(METHODS, names(w)))]
  names(w)[1:2] <- c("Data", "Position")
  w$Data[duplicated(w$Data)] <- ""
  cat(tab(w, digits = 0, caption = sprintf("%s: coverage (%%) of the %d days after the window", M, H)), sep = "\n")
}
```

## By wave

```{r by-wave, results="asis"}
for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) {
  a <- aggregate(coverage ~ wave + method, res[res$model == M, ], mean)
  w <- reshape(a, idvar = "wave", timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("^coverage\\.", "", names(w))

}
```

## Utah COVID-19

The two Utah COVID-19 datasets on their own: the last year of the Utah data (2024-25) and the
summer 2023 wave. Coverage (%) of the observed daily cases by window position (mean over the
window lengths), and the interval score.

```{r utah, results="asis"}
U <- c("Utah COVID-19 2024-25", "Utah COVID-19 summer 2023")
for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) for (what in c("coverage", "interval_score")) {
  a <- aggregate(as.formula(paste(what, "~ wave + position + method")), res[res$model == M & res$wave %in% U, ], mean)
  w <- reshape(a, idvar = c("wave", "position"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub(paste0("^", what, "\\."), "", names(w))
  w <- w[order(match(w$wave, U), match(w$position, POSITIONS)), c("wave", "position", intersect(METHODS, names(w)))]
  names(w)[1:2] <- c("Data", "Position")
  w$Data[duplicated(w$Data)] <- ""
  cat(tab(w, digits = if (what == "coverage") 0 else 1,
          caption = sprintf("%s, Utah COVID-19: %s by window position", M, if (what == "coverage") "coverage (%)" else "interval score")), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Examples

The `r L_SHOW`-day windows (rows: waves; columns: beginning, middle, end). Blue: observed;
green: the BiLSTM's 95% band and median; red dashed: ABC-MCMC; gold dotted: DE. Panel titles:
coverage of BiLSTM | ABC-MCMC | DE.

```{r examples, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, results="asis"}
show <- intersect(c("New York", "Texas", "North Dakota"), STATES_USED)
groups <- c(lapply(show, function(s) grep(paste0("^", s, " "), names(waves), value = TRUE)),
            list(c("Utah COVID-19 2024-25", "Utah COVID-19 summer 2023"),
                 c("Utah flu 2022-23", "Utah flu 2023-24", "Baltimore flu 1918")))
names(groups) <- c(show, "Utah COVID-19", "Influenza")
for (M in names(MODEL_DIRS)) for (gname in names(groups)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", M, ": ", gname, "\n\n", sep = "")
  op <- par(mfrow = c(length(groups[[gname]]), 3), mar = c(2.5, 4, 3, 0.5))
  for (wv in groups[[gname]]) for (pos in POSITIONS) {
    w <- Filter(function(z) z$wave == wv && z$length == L_SHOW && z$position == pos, windows)
    if (!length(w)) { plot.new(); next }
    w <- w[[1]]
    f <- lapply(setNames(METHODS, METHODS), function(m) readRDS(fit_file(M, w$id, m)))
    top <- max(c(w$y, f$BiLSTM$band$upper[seq_len(w$length)], pmin(f$`ABC-MCMC`$band$upper[seq_len(w$length)], 2.5 * max(w$y))))
    plot(w$x, w$y, type = "n", ylim = c(0, top), xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", cex.main = 0.85,
         main = sprintf("%s, %s\n%.0f%% | %.0f%% | %.0f%%", wv, pos, f$BiLSTM$window[["coverage"]],
                        f$`ABC-MCMC`$window[["coverage"]], f$DE$window[["coverage"]]))
    i <- seq_len(w$length); b <- f$BiLSTM$band[i, ]
    polygon(c(w$x, rev(w$x)), c(b$upper, rev(b$lower)), col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", 0.3), border = NA)
    lines(w$x, b$median, col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2)
    lines(w$x, f$`ABC-MCMC`$band$upper[i], col = "firebrick", lty = 2); lines(w$x, f$`ABC-MCMC`$band$lower[i], col = "firebrick", lty = 2)
    lines(w$x, f$DE$band$upper[i], col = "goldenrod", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5); lines(w$x, f$DE$band$lower[i], col = "goldenrod", lty = 3, lwd = 1.5)
    lines(w$x, w$y, col = "blue", lwd = 1.3)
  }
  par(op)
}
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(OUT_DIR, "session_info.txt"))
```
